questions.question: According to John Locke, which is NOT a natural right? / a). Life b). Liberty c). Property d). Punishment
questions.solution_html: Correct Option: Option (d) Punishment

questions.question: Social welfare theory was advocated by __________. / a). Bentham and Mill b). Marx and Engels c). Rousseau and Kant d). Locke and Hobbes
questions.solution_html: Correct Option: Option (a) Bentham and Mill

questions.question: Trade unions fight for: / a). Lower wages b). Workers’ c). Child labor d). Exploitation welfare
questions.solution_html: Correct Option: Option (b) Workers’ welfare

questions.question: International human rights law applies during a). Peace only b). War only c). Peace and d). Emergencies conflict only
questions.solution_html: Correct Option: Option (c) Peace and conflict

questions.question: The UN Declaration on Minority Rights was adopted in __________. / a). 1948 b). 1966 c). 1992 d). 2000
questions.solution_html: Correct Option: Option (c) 1992

questions.solution_html: Climate change reporting creates awareness and encourages action.
questions.final_answer: Climate change reporting creates awareness and encourages action

questions.question: Name any two rights mentioned in the Declaration of the Rights of Man.
questions.solution_html: Liberty, Equality, Property, Security (any two).

questions.question: How can the Right to Information conflict with the Right to Privacy?
questions.solution_html:
• RTI promotes transparency while privacy protects personal information-Conflict

questions.final_answer: RTI promotes transparency while privacy protects personal information-Conflict

questions.question: Explain the historical and intellectual foundations of human rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Historical and intellectual foundations of human rights
  • Natural rights theory - Magna Carta -French Revolution - Universal Declaration
  • of Human Rights -Thinkers like Locke, Rousseau etc.
questions.final_answer: of Human Rights -Thinkers like Locke, Rousseau etc

questions.question: Discuss surveillance as a modern pathology of human rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Surveillance as a modern pathology of human rights
  • Meaning of surveillance - Digital monitoring and data collection - Privacy
  • violations -Government and corporate surveillance -Need for legal safeguards
questions.final_answer: violations -Government and corporate surveillance -Need for legal safeguards

questions.question: Describe the human rights issues of elderly people and how media creates awareness about them.
questions.solution_html:
• Human rights issues of elderly people and media awareness. –
  • Neglect and abuse-Health and financial insecurity - Social isolation - Role of
  • media campaigns and awareness programmes - Government welfare schemes

questions.question: What is digital media literacy? Explain why it is important for protecting human rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Digital media literacy and protection of human rights
  • Meaning of digital media literacy -Identifying fake news and misinformation
  • Safe online behaviour - Protection of privacy and freedom of expression
  • Responsible digital citizenship.
